recognize_zh: 大量細胞的細胞核呈雙葉、蝴蝶形或腎形折疊（bilobed / butterfly nuclei），細胞質淡灰藍色、只有細小粉塵狀顆粒，缺乏典型粗大嗜天青顆粒，符合微顆粒型急性前骨髓細胞白血病（APL, microgranular variant）；外觀易與單核球混淆。
features: Sheets of medium to large cells with moderate N:C ratio
Characteristic bilobed, butterfly-shaped, folded or reniform nuclei
Fine chromatin with small nucleoli in some cells
Pale gray-blue cytoplasm with sparse fine dust-like azurophilic granules
Few mature granulocytes; scattered basophilic erythroid precursors/lymphocytes
describe_en: Smear shows a predominance of medium to large abnormal cells with bilobed, butterfly-shaped or deeply folded nuclei, fine chromatin and occasional small nucleoli. The cytoplasm is pale gray-blue with only sparse, fine dust-like granules, and coarse granules or Auer rod bundles are not conspicuous in this field. Normal hematopoietic elements are reduced. Findings are consistent with the microgranular (hypogranular) variant of acute promyelocytic leukemia; urgent coagulation studies and PML-RARA testing are indicated, and strong MPO positivity helps separate it from monocytic leukemia.

ddx.vs: Monoblasts/promonocytes also have folded nuclei but are MPO weak/negative, nonspecific esterase positive and HLA-DR/CD14 positive, whereas microgranular APL is strongly MPO positive and HLA-DR negative with PML-RARA.
Classic APL shows abundant coarse azurophilic granules obscuring the nucleus and faggot cells, whereas the microgranular variant has fine dust-like granules and a markedly elevated WBC.
NPM1-mutated AML blasts may show nuclear invaginations and HLA-DR negativity, but lack bilobed butterfly nuclei and PML-RARA, requiring molecular confirmation.
